subject.title: [Bug]: gateway.nodes.denyCommands silently accepts invalid command names without warning

question: Should `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` config writes warn and continue, fail closed, or stay audit-only when entries are unknown, pattern-like, or provided by plugins/custom nodes?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the security/product contract is not: fail-closed validation improves safety for typos while warning-only behavior avoids blocking valid plugin or future node command IDs.

options.title: Warn and continue
options.body: Emit write-time warnings for unknown or pattern-like deny entries using the audit vocabulary, but keep the write valid so plugin/custom command IDs are not blocked.

options.title: Fail closed
options.body: Reject unknown or pattern-like deny entries at config write time, accepting the compatibility risk for plugin/custom commands unless a registry-aware exemption is added first.

options.title: Stay audit-only
options.body: Keep config writes permissive and rely on `openclaw security audit` to report ineffective deny entries after the fact.

recommendation.title: Warn and continue
recommendation.body: Emit write-time warnings for unknown or pattern-like deny entries using the audit vocabulary, but keep the write valid so plugin/custom command IDs are not blocked.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects security posture and gateway command policy semantics, and this history points to recent denyCommands/security policy ownership.
